articles.title: Draft NUREG: Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities
articles.summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing for public comment a draft report entitled, NUREG-1307, Revision 21, "Report on Waste Burial Charges: Changes in Decommissioning Waste Disposal Costs at Low-Level Waste Burial Facilities." This report, which is revised periodically, explains the formula acceptable to the NRC for determining the minimum decommissioning fund requirements for nuclear power reactor licensees, as required by NRC regulations. Specifically, this report provides the adjustment factor and updates the values for the labor, energy, and waste burial escalation factors of the minimum formula.

The concession can run for up to 25 years, although final administrative approval is still required before the new agreement becomes effective. AG Seville Shipyard faced competition for the facilities from Spanish maritime group Boluda, which had also expressed interest in taking over the site. The successful operator has controlled part of the former Seville shipyard since 2017, developing ship repair and maintenance operations at facilities that had suffered years of decline following the collapse of the former public shipyard. The company plans to invest approximately €10m ($11.2m) in modernisation and expansion projects under the new concession. articles.content: Iraqi Line returns to Gulf container trade after 50 years - Splash247 ICTSI Iraq’s national shipping line is returning to scheduled container services in the Gulf after more than half a century, as the country seeks to rebuild maritime connections disrupted by the Strait of Hormuz crisis. According to Alphaliner, Iraqi Maritime Line is deploying the 902 teu Basrah on an eight-day shuttle linking Jebel Ali in Dubai with Umm Qasr, Iraq’s principal container gateway. The first sailing was scheduled to depart Jebel Ali yesterday, arriving in Umm Qasr two days later. Iraq’s transport ministry has described the initiative as the national carrier’s first regular Gulf operation since the mid-1960s. The relaunch comes as Iraqi container supply chains have been radically reshaped since the Hormuz shipping crisis erupted at the end of February. Growing volumes have been diverted to Jordan’s Red Sea port of Aqaba before travelling overland into Iraq through the Trebil border crossing. According to the Jordan Shipping Association, Aqaba handled 37,182 Iraq-bound transit containers during the first seven months of 2026, compared with just 3,599 during the corresponding period last year, a 933% increase. Maersk has introduced landbridge services connecting Aqaba with Iraq, while CMA CGM has offered alternative routings through Aqaba for southern Iraq and Turkey’s Mersin for northern destinations. articles.content: Gestion Maritime makes ultramax debut with China order - Splash247 Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering Monaco-based shipowner Gestion Maritime is moving into the ultramax segment with an order for three 64,000 dwt bulk carriers at China’s Nantong Xiangyu Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering. The Danilo Fumarola-led company has booked the trio for delivery between late 2028 and early 2029, expanding beyond its traditional panamax and kamsarmax fleet. The vessels are costing in the low $30m range apiece, putting the overall investment at more than $90m. Gestion Maritime currently operates six panamax and kamsarmax bulkers and has recently trimmed its fleet through asset sales. The latest investment will bring smaller and more modern tonnage into a portfolio built largely around Japanese- and South Korean-built ships. The company, whose roots date back to 1908 and the Corrado shipping family, has traditionally pursued an asset trading strategy, buying ships when values ease and disposing of tonnage during stronger markets. In 2019, it exited the product tanker sector by selling two 2015-built MR tankers to Hafnia interests for $31m each, returning its focus to dry bulk. The newbuilding deal adds another international owner to Nantong Xiangyu’s growing customer base. The Chinese shipbuilder marked the delivery of its 100th ultramax bulker in July and has continued to attract orders for the 63,500 to 64,000 dwt segment. articles.content: Aker BP and Höegh Evi secure EU funding for North Sea CO2 storage project - Splash247 Aker BP Norwegian offshore producer Aker BP and maritime infrastructure specialist Höegh Evi have secured €223m ($260m) from the European Union Innovation Fund for their Atlas carbon transport and storage project in the North Sea. The project aims to establish a large-scale carbon capture and storage (CCS) network that links industrial emitters across Europe to permanent storage facilities on the Norwegian continental shelf through a combination of collection hubs, specialised CO2 carriers, and subsea injection infrastructure. Atlas has an initial design capacity of 6m tonnes of CO2 annually, with potential to expand beyond 10m tonnes as the European carbon storage market develops. Under the proposed system, the project would aggregate captured CO2 at regional export hubs near industrial clusters before transporting it aboard dedicated low-pressure carriers to the offshore storage site. CO2 would be injected directly through subsea infrastructure into a saline aquifer more than 2,000 m below the seabed, removing the need for extensive onshore pipeline networks. The project was recognised as an EU Project of Mutual Interest in April 2026, acknowledging its potential to provide cross-border carbon transport and storage infrastructure. articles.content: Trump’s Plan to Revive Sanctioned Tankers Faces Tough Sell Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins Trump’s Plan to Revive Sanctioned Tankers Faces Tough Sell Bloomberg Total Views: 271 October 20, 2026 (Bloomberg) — A US plan to rehabilitate sanctioned tankers to boost oil supply may attract only a sliver of the dark fleet, as existing contracts, complex compliance checks and sky-high freight rates reduce incentives for would-be sellers. The measure — detailed on Monday, just weeks ahead of the US midterm elections — is the latest in a string of efforts by the Trump administration to cool crude and fuel prices driven higher by months of war in the Persian Gulf and the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine. Soaring gasoline and diesel costs in particular have fueled affordability concerns among US voters. articles.content: MSC tipped for another 20 megamaxes in China - Splash247 Yangzijiang Shipbuilding Mediterranean Shipping Co (MSC) has reportedly added another 20 megamax containerships at China’s Hengli Heavy Industries, further expanding its already massive orderbook as global newbuilding commitments climb to their highest level in more than a decade. According to liner consultancy Linerlytica, Gianluigi Aponte’s carrier has booked 20 additional 24,000 teu vessels at the Dalian-based shipbuilder, representing another 480,000 teu of future capacity. The latest deal takes MSC’s programme of vessels exceeding 20,000 teu at Hengli to 62 ships, Linerlytica said in its latest weekly market report. No contract value, delivery dates or propulsion specifications have been disclosed for the new batch. MSC has built up a substantial pipeline at Hengli since the two companies signed a strategic cooperation agreement in 2024. The liner giant initially contracted ten 21,000 teu and ten 24,000 teu LNG dual-fuel newbuildings, before returning for six 22,000 teu ships last year. The latest reported order adds another sizeable block of capacity to an expansion programme that already dwarfs those of rival carriers. At the end of September, Alphaliner data cited by Splash put MSC’s operated fleet at around 7.4m teu, representing 21.5% of global liner capacity, with another 2.94m teu on order. articles.content: Spodumene shipments triple as battery boom creates new dry bulk trades - Splash247 Tata Motors The seaborne trade in spodumene, a lithium-bearing mineral essential for battery production, is emerging as one of dry bulk shipping’s fastest-growing niche cargoes, with volumes more than tripling over the past five years. New research from Greek shipbroker Ursa Shipbrokers shows global shipments reached 4.04m tonnes in the first nine months of 2026, up 11.9% year-on-year and a record for the period. Annual shipments have climbed from just 1.58m tonnes in 2020 to 5.08m tonnes last year, reflecting the rapid expansion of lithium mining and growing demand from electric vehicle manufacturers and battery storage projects. Australia dominates the trade, accounting for 81% of shipments during the first nine months of this year, equivalent to 3.26m tonnes. Brazil ranked second with 570,000 tonnes, while smaller quantities originated in Canada, Mozambique and Vietnam. China remains overwhelmingly the principal destination, receiving 88% of global seaborne spodumene cargoes, equivalent to 3.56m tonnes, reflecting its dominant position in lithium refining and battery manufacturing. The trade is providing growing employment opportunities for smaller bulk carriers. Ultramaxes accounted for 39.6% of vessel deadweight employed in spodumene shipments this year, with handysizes representing a further 46%. articles.content: Apache braces for offshore strike across seven platforms - Splash247 Apache More than 160 offshore workers, employed by US oil and gas producer Apache, are set to stage a 24-hour strike across seven North Sea installations on Wednesday, with union Unite warning the industrial action could disrupt the strategically important Forties Pipeline System. The walkout will begin at 6 am on October 21 and end the following morning. A second 24-hour stoppage is scheduled for November 4. The affected installations are Forties Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta, and Echo, alongside Beryl Alpha and Beryl Bravo. Unite said shutting down the Forties Charlie platform could drop pipeline pressure, potentially forcing the entire Ineos-operated Forties Pipeline System (FPS) offline and disrupting production from other North Sea operators. The FPS handles oil and gas liquids from more than 80 offshore fields and the St Fergus gas terminal, with a nominal capacity exceeding 600,000 barrels per day. Apache, however, has rejected suggestions that the strike could shut down the wider network. The company said contingency plans included retaining experienced personnel on Forties Charlie to support third-party production, even if output from all five Apache-operated Forties platforms was suspended. Apache maintained that any resulting pressure reduction would be comparable to a routine maintenance shutdown. The dispute centres on a pay offer that Unite claims amounts to a real-terms pay cut for many workers

articles.content: Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins Greece Says It is Implementing Sanctions Linked to Iran Reuters Total Views: 61 October 22, 2026 ATHENS, Oct 22 (Reuters) – The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism. The statement comes after the US Treasury Department said on Wednesday it imposed sanctions on Karnakis & Karnakis, a law firm based in Greece and Panama, saying it had for years provided legal assistance to Iranian shipping networks. The Treasury also said that the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued an administrative subpoena to advance an investigation into a Greek bank, which it did not name. The Greek finance ministry said it had taken note of the US Treasury statement, adding that “all available information is being evaluated, and appropriate measures are being taken in accordance with established procedures and applicable national, EU, and international law.” (Reporting by Angeliki Koutantou; Editing by Aidan Lewis) (c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026. articles.content: US sanctions net widens to shipping agents and lawyers - Splash247 Washington.org Washington has widened its crackdown on Iran’s shadow fleet, sanctioning a Greek-Panamanian law firm, shipping agents in Singapore and Dubai, and nine vessels in a move targeting the service providers behind Tehran’s commodity exports. Announcing the measures yesterday, the US Treasury said Karnakis and Karnakis had established corporate structures for shipowners moving hundreds of millions of dollars worth of Iranian oil, LPG, petrochemicals and steel. Five individuals linked to the practice have also been designated. OK By Oh Seok-min SEOUL, Oct. 22 (Yonhap) -- Cuba is seeking to deepen economic ties with South Korea as it has been grappling with the economic and energy crises exacerbated by decadeslong U.S. sanctions on Havana, the Cuban ambassador to Seoul has said. General Assembly on Cuba's annual resolution calling for an end to the U.S. embargo. (Yonhap) "There has been a constant trickle of new measures and sanctions that affect both the public and private sectors," Monzon said. The ambassador said intensified U.S. sanctions have had far-reaching effects on Cuba's trade, fuel supplies and public services, including healthcare. "If not the worst, it's at least one of the worst situations we've been through," he said. Cuba has submitted an annual resolution against the U.S. embargo since 1992, and this year will be no exception, with a vote scheduled for Oct. 27-28. "

articles.content: China's green corridor push hits commercial reality check - Splash247 CMB.TECH China has emerged as a major player in the global green shipping corridor movement, with at least 21 initiatives linked to the country, although most remain in their early stages and only one has progressed towards commercial operation, according to a new report from the Global Maritime Forum. The study, released during the organisation’s annual summit in Shanghai, shows that China accounts for nearly a fifth of the world’s green shipping corridor initiatives, having added ten new projects in 2025 alone. However, of the 21 initiatives identified by the end of June this year, 12 were still at the initiation stage, five were exploring feasibility, three had reached preparation and just one had entered the realisation phase. The most advanced is the Australia-East Asia Iron Ore corridor, involving the deployment of ammonia-powered bulk carriers between Australia’s Pilbara region and China. The report also highlights how much of the sector’s future fuel supply is increasingly concentrated in China. The country accounts for around 80% of global green methanol production capacity that has passed final investment decision and more than 40% of comparable green ammonia capacity. articles.content: VLCC delivery wave set to reach levels not seen since the 1970s - Splash247 Hengli Group The VLCC sector is heading for its biggest delivery wave in half a century, with more than 100 new supertankers scheduled to enter service annually in both 2028 and 2029, according to Hartland Shipping Services. The scale recalls the supertanker boom of the 1970s. BIMCO’s historical figures put the all-time record at 116 VLCCs delivered in 1974. Since then, even the 68 deliveries recorded in 2019 represented a four-decade high. The historical precedent is worth noting. A wave of tankers ordered during the early 1970s boom arrived just as the 1973 oil shock devastated demand. Between 1974 and 1975, global oil trade plunged 23% while tanker capacity grew nearly 16%, according to UNCTAD. Freight rates collapsed. The reopening of the Suez Canal in 1975 further shortened voyages. By year-end, 573 tankers representing 47.8m dwt were laid up, according to INTERTANKO. Owners faced financial ruin, newbuildings went straight into lay-up and the industry endured a prolonged depression. Hartland now counts 319 VLCCs on order, equivalent to 34% of the existing fleet, rising to 42% when sanctioned ships are excluded. Yet just 20 are scheduled for delivery over the next six months. Only six VLCCs delivered last year and just one in 2024. This could be an upcoming supply disaster Of the current orderbook, 138 ships are not due until 2029 or later. articles.content: Trader Alkagesta enters shipowning with Turkish bunker fleet takeover - Splash247 Energy Petrol Malta-based commodities trader Alkagesta is entering shipowning through the acquisition of Turkish marine fuel supplier Energy Petrol, taking over an eight-vessel bunker fleet as it expands its physical fuel distribution business. The Orkhan Rustamov-led company confirmed on October 22 that it had agreed to acquire the Istanbul-based supplier in a transaction already approved by Türkiye’s competition authority. Financial terms have not been disclosed, and Energy Petrol is expected to continue operating independently. The deal marks Alkagesta’s first investment in owned vessels, moving the group beyond fuel trading and chartered shipping into direct physical distribution. Energy Petrol, established in 1997 by Mustafa and Yeşim Muhtaroğlu, is an established bunker supplier in the Turkish Straits region. The company operates bunker tankers supplying marine gasoil and fuel oil, with its fleet including the 3,659 dwt Deniz M, the 2,818 dwt Energy K and smaller vessels serving the Istanbul market. Energy Petrol’s website lists a wider historical fleet, although the companies have not identified which eight vessels are included in the transaction. Ceva Logistics, a top-five global logistics company by gross revenue and part of Marseilles, France-based CMA CGM Group, acquired Paack in early August to expand its last-mile delivery business in Europe. It acquired Colis Privé, which also operates in Belgium and Luxembourg, in 2022. The unified Paack brand will be rolled out progressively to customers and partners beginning in January, Ceva said in a news release. When the tentative deal was first announced last summer, the expectation was that Colis Privé would absorb Paack. Paack has about 490 employees. It also operates six urban delivery stations in France. The couriers also deliver to individual residences. articles.summary:
Drewry’s World Container Index rose on higher rates on trans-Pacific and Asia-Europe routes.
The post New Drewry data shows import demand boosting trans-Pacific rates appeared first on FreightWaves.
articles.content: New Drewry data shows import demand boosting trans-Pacific rates - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Drewry’s World Container Index rose 2% to $4,585 per 40-foot container, supported by higher rates on trans-Pacific and Asia-Europe routes as strong U.S. import demand and carrier capacity cuts bolstered pricing. Shanghai-to-Los Angeles rates increased 2% to $8,007 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-New York rates edged up 1% to $10,166. Drewry expects trans-Pacific rates to remain stable next week, with U.S. import demand continuing to support the market despite an increase in available capacity. Carriers have announced only two blank sailings on the trans-Pacific for next week, down from six this week, according to figures from Drewry’s Container Capacity Insight. The service tracks scheduled and canceled sailings, effective capacity and port congestion across major trade lanes. Rates from Shanghai to Rotterdam rose 3% to $3,632 per 40-foot container, while Shanghai-to-Genoa rates increased 5% to $4,152. Unlike the trans-Pacific, the Asia-Europe trade faces more sailing cancellations next week. Carriers have announced eight blank sailings, up from two this week, tightening available capacity as they seek to put upward pressure on freight rates. articles.content: Workforce gaps keep supply chain AI stuck in pilot mode - FreightWaves Ends Friday 10/23 F3 Promo code: LUCKYLAST50 Register → × Freight technology vendors are selling AI agents that can benchmark rates and award freight under rules a customer sets. A new survey finds most supply chain organizations still limit AI to generating insights, and the first obstacle the research names is their own workforce. The Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute (DSCI) released The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration on Oct. 14. Of the supply chain professionals surveyed, 83% said their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively. The 17% who described their workforce as ready reported a 71% AI project success rate. Everyone else reported 28%, and about 64% of that group is still in the pilot or planning stage. Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM, said most AI sessions at supply chain conferences run through the same agenda: the challenges, the implementation, and the benefits. Every one of them ends with a reminder not to forget about the people, he said. “It’s interesting because from our perspective that’s where you ought to start the conversation,” Eshkenazi told FreightWaves. AI mostly stays in planning The report scored AI adoption across 13 core supply chain functions on a scale from 1, meaning no AI use, to 5, meaning autonomous execution without human review. Hampton, led by chairman and chief executive Peter Deeb, claims Icon has raised approximately $25m through common share issuances since its 2024 flotation, while ordinary shareholders have suffered substantial losses. The Canadian investment firm has also questioned the treatment of preferred shares held by Icon’s controlling shareholder and chief executive, Ismini Panagiotidi. Hampton is proposing that Icon exchange its outstanding Series A preferred shares for a new instrument with a $20m face value, a fixed 6% cash dividend and conversion rights priced at $5 per ordinary share. It also wants a one-for-one share dividend for existing ordinary shareholders and the appointment of a Hampton-nominated director. The order would mark Lavinia’s first move into newcastlemax newbuildings since 2013, when the company contracted six ships of this size. Those vessels remain part of the group’s dry bulk fleet. Lavinia has concentrated much of its recent bulker investment on smaller tonnage. The company booked eight kamsarmax newbuildings during 2023 and 2024 at Chinese yards, including CMI, COSCO Heavy Industry and Jiangsu New Hantong. Five have since joined the fleet, with another three scheduled for 2027.
